FROM debian:bookworm-slim

# Build tools and SDL2 / fheroes2 dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git \
        ca-certificates \
        cmake \
        make \
        g++ \
        libsdl2-dev \
        libsdl2-mixer-dev \
        libsdl2-image-dev \
        libpng-dev \
        zlib1g-dev \
        gettext \
        pkg-config \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# [IMPORTANT] Copy bug patches to a TEMP path (not into /app) so they can be applied
# into the base snapshot below and never reach the agent-visible tree. These live
# outside assets/ (which is exclusively the documented, agent-visible evidence
# directory) so the patches are never mistaken for shipped evidence.
COPY bugs/ /tmp/bugs/

# Clone fheroes2, pin to the base commit, then strip .git (anti-cheat: the agent
# cannot inspect the fix PR or future history).  Apply the additional injected-bug
# patches (on top of the real historical pre-fix commit) before re-initializing a
# single-commit repo tagged harbor_base, so the defects are part of the exact state
# the model starts from and the verifier can reset test files via `git checkout harbor_base`.
RUN git clone https://github.com/ihhub/fheroes2 /app \
    && git -C /app checkout 8ece9d7007c714b749953ab5cd765a271912b06f \
    && rm -rf /app/.git \
    # [IMPORTANT] Apply every bug patch BEFORE the snapshot below, so the defect
    # becomes part of harbor_base (the exact state the model starts from).
    && for p in /tmp/bugs/*.patch; do git -C /app apply "$p" || patch -p1 -d /app < "$p"; done \
    && git -C /app init -q \
    && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
    && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
    # [IMPORTANT] harbor_base = base commit + all bug patches. Must come AFTER the
    # apply loop; the verifier resets to this tag.
    && git -C /app tag harbor_base \
    # [IMPORTANT] Delete the temp copy now that the patches are applied. The COPY
    # above still exists in an earlier layer, but the agent only ever sees the
    # final merged filesystem (CMD is bash), so a live shell can no longer find
    # /tmp/bugs -- and with it, the exact before/after values the bugs corrupted.
    && rm -rf /tmp/bugs

WORKDIR /app

# Prepare log directory and the harbor_assets mount point
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets

# Visual evidence — readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/. The bug patches
# above live outside this directory (environment/bugs/, not environment/assets/),
# so nothing here needs to be scrubbed before it reaches the agent.
# tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image;
# the harness supplies them at verify time.
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

5	# compiles the test against the CANDIDATE's dialog_selectscenario.cpp,

9	# whether fheroes2::showMessage was invoked — it NEVER greps source code.
10	#
11	# BASE  (no fix) : ActionListPressRight calls showMessage → test FAILS → reward 0.0
12	# FIXED (fix app): ActionListPressRight is a no-op → test PASSES    → reward 1.0
13	set -uo pipefail
14	
15	mkdir -p /logs/verifier
16	STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
17	STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
18	REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
19	
20	: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
21	: > "$STDERR_LOG"
22	
23	ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
24	trap ensure_reward EXIT
25	
26	cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
27	
28	# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
29	# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
30	#
31	# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
32	# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
33	#
34	# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx
35	# in-tree AFTER the harbor_base commit (environment/Dockerfile), so everything the build
36	# emits is untracked and NOT in wx's .gitignore. A bare `add -A` captured 380MB of .o/.d/.so;
37	# excluding those by extension still left ~120 configure-generated files (samples/*/Makefile,
38	# bk-deps, version-script, lib/wx/config/*, the utils/wxrc/wxrc binary) because most have no
39	# extension to blacklist. Inverting it -- stage tracked modifications, then add only untracked
40	# files that LOOK like source -- keeps the agent's work and drops generated output by default.
41	_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
42	_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
43	_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
44	         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
45	rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
46	GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
47	GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
48	# Enumerate before adding: `git add` aborts and stages NOTHING if any one pathspec matches
49	# no file, which silently drops the agent's new files on most tasks.
50	# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
51	# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above
52	# already has them. This drops only files CREATED under a build dir during the run -- which,
53	# left in, break replay: they are recorded as new-file hunks and a fresh container from the
54	# same image already has them, so `git apply` fails with "already exists in working directory".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for ihhub__fheroes2-4924-mm.
#
# Applies the test patch (adds stubs.cpp + test_actionlistpressright.cpp),
# compiles the test against the CANDIDATE's dialog_selectscenario.cpp,
# links with GoogleTest, runs the test, and calls verifier.py.
#
# BEHAVIORAL: the test calls ScenarioListBox::ActionListPressRight() and checks
# whether fheroes2::showMessage was invoked — it NEVER greps source code.
#
# BASE  (no fix) : ActionListPressRight calls showMessage → test FAILS → reward 0.0
# FIXED (fix app): ActionListPressRight is a no-op → test PASSES    → reward 1.0
set -uo pipefail

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
: > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
#
# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
#
# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx
# in-tree AFTER the harbor_base commit (environment/Dockerfile), so everything the build
# emits is untracked and NOT in wx's .gitignore. A bare `add -A` captured 380MB of .o/.d/.so;
# excluding those by extension still left ~120 configure-generated files (samples/*/Makefile,
# bk-deps, version-script, lib/wx/config/*, the utils/wxrc/wxrc binary) because most have no
# extension to blacklist. Inverting it -- stage tracked modifications, then add only untracked
# files that LOOK like source -- keeps the agent's work and drops generated output by default.
_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
# Enumerate before adding: `git add` aborts and stages NOTHING if any one pathspec matches
# no file, which silently drops the agent's new files on most tasks.
# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above
# already has them. This drops only files CREATED under a build dir during the run -- which,
# left in, break replay: they are recorded as new-file hunks and a fresh container from the
# same image already has them, so `git apply` fails with "already exists in working directory".
mapfile -t _SUBNEW < <(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard \
  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -- "${_SUBNEW[@]}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app diff --binary --cached harbor_base \
  > "$_SUB" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"

# WHAT THE WHITELIST DROPPED, listed rather than silently discarded. The split above captures
# every change to a TRACKED file (any extension, deletions included) but only NEW files that
# look like source -- so an agent adding config.yml, a .cmake module or an extensionless script
# loses it, and the patch still looks clean. That is the failure this manifest exists to expose.
#
# NEWEST FIRST, which is the useful ordering and not a cosmetic one: build output and image
# assets are created before the agent phase starts, so anything the agent made sorts to the top.
# Build artifacts are excluded by the same rules as the capture, to keep the list readable.
#
# If something here belongs in the submission, widen _SUBSRC. Do not reach for `add -A`.
_SUBSKIP=/logs/verifier/submission-skipped.txt
_SUBCAP=/tmp/.submission_captured
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "${_SUBNEW[@]}" > "$_SUBCAP"; else : > "$_SUBCAP"; fi
_SUBSKIPN=$(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
{ echo "# Untracked files NOT captured into submission.patch, newest first."
  echo "# Anything the agent created sorts above build output, which predates the agent phase."
  echo "# total: ${_SUBSKIPN}  (showing at most 40)"
  git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
      ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
      ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
      ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | head -200 \
    | while IFS= read -r _f; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(stat -c %Y "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
                              "$(stat -c %s "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$_f"
      done \
    | sort -rn | head -40 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n",$1,$2,$3}'
} > "$_SUBSKIP" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$_SUBCAP"

# Size guard. The whitelist is a heuristic, so a task laying out source unusually could still
# produce something enormous. Cap it and leave a diagnosable stub: a truncated capture is
# recoverable, a full disk is not.
_SUBSZ=$(wc -c < "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$_SUBSZ" -gt 5242880 ]; then
  { echo "SUBMISSION CAPTURE SUPPRESSED: ${_SUBSZ} bytes exceeds the 5MB cap."
    echo "Directories contributing to the discarded patch:"
    grep -a "^diff --git" "$_SUB" | sed 's#^diff --git a/##; s# b/.*##; s#/[^/]*$##' \
      | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
  } > "$_SUB.suppressed" 2>/dev/null
  : > "$_SUB"
  echo "== submission.patch SUPPRESSED (${_SUBSZ} bytes > 5MB cap) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
else
  echo "== captured submission.patch (${_SUBSZ} bytes, $(grep -ac '^diff --git' "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) files) ==" \
    | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1 — reset test-patch paths from harbor_base so the apply is idempotent
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u) 2>/dev/null || true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2 — apply test.patch (adds harbor_test_src/ test files)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# no network: this is plain GoogleTest source, not a Debian package, and it
# is never baked into the agent-visible image -- only /tests/ carries it,

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    && rm -rf "$GTEST_BUILD_DIR" \
    || { echo "ERROR: could not build libgtest.a from /tests/vendor/googletest" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
fi

  || { echo "ERROR: libgtest.a not found" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

  -I /app/src/fheroes2/ai
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/army
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/battle
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/campaign
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/castle
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/dialog
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/game
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/gui
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/h2d
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/heroes
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/image
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/kingdom
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/maps
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/monster
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/objects
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/pocketpc
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/resource
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/spell
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/system
  -I /app/src/fheroes2/world

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
verifier.py — parses GoogleTest JUnit XML output and writes a reward.

Reward policy is BINARY, never partial credit:
  1.0 — every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes (or p2p is empty) AND the
        rubric (if any verdict is available) did not fail
  0.0 — anything short of that: no f2p passes, a strict subset of f2p passes, a p2p
        regression, report missing / failed to parse, or a failed rubric

The rubric can only ever withhold a 1.0, never turn a genuine 0.0 result into something
worse, and a missing/unavailable rubric verdict never blocks a 1.0.

This task has:
  f2p = ["ScenarioListBox.IconAreaRightClickDoesNotShowPopup"]
  p2p = []  (no pre-existing tests to guard)
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P  = CONF['f2p']
P2P  = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'

# --- canonical reward writer + --rubric gate (see RUBRIC_MODES.md §2) --------------
# reward.json MUST be a FLAT map of numbers, exactly these seven keys:
#     {reward, tests_passed, f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric_passed}
# harbor parses it as dict[str, float | int] and prefers it over reward.txt; a nested
# value raises a validation error before any reward is recorded. rubric_passed: 1 pass /
# 0 fail / -1 not graded. Registered with atexit so it writes last.
_CANON_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'
_CANON_TXT = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        'reward': 0.0 if rubric == 'fail' else tests_passed,
        'tests_passed': tests_passed,
        'f2p_passed': f, 'f2p_total': t,
        'p2p_passed': p, 'p2p_total': q,
        'rubric_passed': {'pass': 1, 'fail': 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon['reward']


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, 'w') as fh:
            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)
        with open(_CANON_TXT, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(str(_canon['reward']))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"WARNING: could not write {_CANON_JSON}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)


def load_results():
    """Return {test_identifier: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as exc:
        print(f"[verifier] XML parse error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        classname = tc.get('classname', '')
        name      = tc.get('name', '')
        # GoogleTest JUnit XML uses '.' as separator in classname; normalise to '::'
        dotted    = f"{classname}.{name}".strip('.')
        colon     = f"{classname}::{name}".strip(':')
        failed    = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped   = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)
        status    = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
        results[dotted]  = status
        results[colon]   = status
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier to a result (substring / regex tolerant)."""
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next(
            (v for k, v in results.items()
             if ident in k or re.search(re.escape(ident), k)),
            None,
        )
        out[ident] = hit or 'missing'
    return out


def parse_rubric_arg(argv):
    """--rubric "pass"|"fail"|"" -> "pass"/"fail"/None. None (missing/unrecognised/empty)
    means no verdict is available yet and must never withhold a 1.0."""
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


def main():
    rubric = parse_rubric_arg(sys.argv[1:])

    r    = load_results()
    f2p  = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p  = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']

    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P), len(p2p_pass), len(P2P), rubric)

    # per-test detail rides along as extra scalar keys on the same flat dict
    for name, v in f2p.items():
        _canon[f'f2p::{name}'] = 1.0 if v == 'pass' else 0.0
    for name, v in p2p.items():
        _canon[f'p2p::{name}'] = 1.0 if v == 'pass' else 0.0

    print(json.dumps({'reward': reward, 'rubric': rubric, 'f2p': f2p, 'p2p': p2p,
                       'report_keys': list(r.keys())}))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Rubric judge — API backend, with the sub-agent backend as fallback.

Binary and unweighted: every criterion is PASS/FAIL and every one is mandatory, so the
rubric passes only if all pass.

Backend selection, in order:

  API (preferred, in-band)
      When EVAL_API_KEY and EVAL_BASE_URL are set, grade the criteria in one
      chat-completions call to the LiteLLM proxy, write the resulting scores map to
      verdict.json in the judge dir, then score it through the SAME read_verdict path the
      sub-agent backend uses -- so the binary / all-mandatory / "not graded == fail"
      semantics are identical whichever backend produced the verdict.

      Requires verifier-phase egress to whatever EVAL_BASE_URL points at. Harbor offers no
      run-level override for the verifier phase (resolve_verifier_phase_policy does no
      extra-host merge and there is no --allow-verifier-host flag), and allowed_hosts is
      validated as literal hostnames and never env-expanded -- so an allowlist would mean
      hardcoding the endpoint into every task. task.toml therefore declares:

          [verifier]
          network_mode = "public"

      The agent phase stays closed; its model host is injected at run time instead.

      Any failure here -- unset key, blocked egress, HTTP error, unparseable response --
      falls through to the sub-agent request below. The judge must never fail the run.

  Sub-agent (fallback, out-of-band)

  Phase 1 (during the verifier run)
      No verdict exists yet, so this writes a self-contained judge request into the judge
      dir -- criteria_payload.json, source.txt (the candidate diff), changed_files.txt (the
      FULL text of every file the diff touched), and PROMPT.md -- prints nothing, and exits 0.
      The verifier then scores on tests alone.

      What the judge deliberately does NOT get: the task instruction (a criterion that has to
      defer to the prompt is a Major "not self-contained" rubric defect -- handing the judge the
      prompt would let such a criterion pass and hide the defect), the golden solution/fix.patch
      (seeing it turns
      the judge into a similarity checker, reintroducing the very overfitting the rubric exists
      to catch), the tests/test.patch (same failure mode, and the tests already score that),
      the before/after images (UI-evaluation criteria are out of scope by definition), and
      browse access to the wider repo (unavailable at rescore time, so it would work in phase 1
      and silently not in phase 2).

  Phase 2 (after the run, orchestrated outside the container)
      A judge sub-agent reads PROMPT.md and writes verdict.json next to it. Re-running this
      script (or `mm_run.sh <task> rescore`) reads that verdict and prints "pass" or "fail".

Contract (test.sh and verifier.py depend on all four):
  * prints "pass" or "fail" on stdout, or NOTHING when no verdict is available yet.
    stdout is captured verbatim into test.sh's RUBRIC, so every diagnostic goes to stderr.
  * writes the per-criterion detail to <judge dir>/summary.json
  * writes {"failed": [...]} to /logs/verifier/rubric.json, which is the path verifier.py
    actually reads for rubric_failed_count (it previously only ever found summary.json in
    the judge dir, so that count was structurally always 0)
  * ALWAYS exits 0, so the judge can never fail the run

Env:
  EVAL_API_KEY      LiteLLM proxy key; absent => skip the API backend entirely
  EVAL_BASE_URL     OpenAI-compatible base, already ending in /v1
  EVAL_MODEL        model name as registered on the proxy
  EVAL_USER         optional; sent as the request's `user` so the proxy can attribute spend
  PB_JUDGE_DIR      where the request/verdict live (default /logs/verifier/judge)
  PB_JUDGE_VERDICT  explicit path to verdict.json (overrides the default location)

Only the stdlib is used for the HTTP call: the verifier image is node:22-bookworm with no
pip install step, so requests/httpx are not available.

IMPORTANT: never name a file in tests/ after a stdlib module (select.py, json.py, types.py,
io.py, queue.py). It shadows the real module and the failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.
The sys.path strip below defends against it.

import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR = "/logs/verifier/judge"
# verifier.py reads this exact path for rubric_failed_count.
RUBRIC_JSON_PATH = "/logs/verifier/rubric.json"
# Bounded well inside the 2400s verifier timeout even in the worst case
# (API_ATTEMPTS * API_TIMEOUT_SEC + backoff).
API_TIMEOUT_SEC = 300
API_ATTEMPTS = 3
# Hunks for these paths never reach the judge: it must grade the fix, not the harness the
# submission may have edited.
EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(
    # Widened beyond the original JS/TS-only patterns. Measured against the corpus, the
    # old form let test files through on 13 tasks -- notably harbor's OWN generated
    # `harbor_test.js` (underscore, not `.test.js`), plus `test_*.cpp`, `*_test.go` and
    # `test_*.py`. A judge that can see the graded tests grades similarity to them, which
    # is the overfitting the rubric exists to catch.
    r"(\.test\.[jt]sx?$|\.spec\.[jt]sx?$"
    r"|_test\.(js|jsx|ts|tsx|py|go|cpp|cc|c|java|kt)$"
    r"|(^|/)test_[^/]+\.(py|cpp|cc|c)$"
    r"|(^|/)jest\.config\.[jt]s$|(^|/)vitest\.config\.[jt]s$"
    r"|(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)__tests__/|(^|/)__snapshots__/"
    r"|(^|/)node_modules/|(^|/)\.git/)"
)
BASE_REFS = ("harbor_base", "HEAD")

JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
    "You are a strict senior engineer grading the APPROACH of a code change -- not whether "
    "its tests pass. Score each rubric criterion STRICTLY BINARY: 1 = fully satisfied, "
    "0 = not satisfied. There is NO partial credit: if a criterion is only partially met, "
    "ambiguous, or has no clear evidence, score 0. Be strict; when unsure, score 0."
)


def judge_dir() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_DIR") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR)


def candidate_diff(repo: str, budget: int = 120_000) -> str:
    for ref in BASE_REFS:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", ref],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git diff failed: %s\n" % exc)
            return ""
        if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] diffing against %s\n" % ref)
            return filter_diff(out.stdout, budget)
        # Surface WHY a ref produced nothing. A non-zero git exit here (bad ref, dubious
        # ownership, corrupt index) is indistinguishable from "the agent changed nothing"
        # unless we say so, and it silently skips rubric grading entirely.
        if out.returncode != 0:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] git diff %s exited %d: %s\n"
                % (ref, out.returncode, (out.stderr or "").strip()[:300])
            )
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] no non-empty diff found against any of %s\n"
                     % ", ".join(BASE_REFS))
    return ""


def filter_diff(diff: str, budget: int) -> str:
    kept, cur, keep = [], [], True
    for line in diff.splitlines(keepends=True):
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            if keep and cur:
                kept.extend(cur)
            parts = line.split()
            path = parts[-1][2:] if len(parts) >= 4 else ""
            keep = not EXCLUDE_RE.search(path)
            cur = [line]
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if keep and cur:
        kept.extend(cur)
    blob = "".join(kept)
    return blob[:budget] + "\n[... truncated ...]\n" if len(blob) > budget else blob


def changed_paths(diff: str) -> list:
    """Paths touched by the (already harness-filtered) diff, in order."""
    out = []
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                p = parts[-1][2:]                  # strip the b/ prefix
                if p and p not in out:
                    out.append(p)
    return out


def collect_changed_files(repo: str, diff: str, budget: int = 200_000) -> str:
    """Full current text of every file the diff touched.

    A hunk shows three lines of context, which is often too little to decide a criterion that
    is genuinely true of the change (e.g. "the helper is defined in the same module"). Whole
    files remove that class of false 0 while staying bounded by the size of the change.
    """
    blob, used = [], 0
    for rel in changed_paths(diff):
        fp = Path(repo) / rel
        if not fp.is_file():                       # deleted or renamed away
            continue
        try:
            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            continue
        chunk = "\n===== %s =====\n%s" % (rel, text)
        if used + len(chunk) > budget:
            blob.append("\n[... remaining changed files omitted for length ...]\n")
            break
        blob.append(chunk); used += len(chunk)
    return "".join(blob)


def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path, changed: str = "") -> None:
    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context."""
    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff)
    extra = []
    if changed.strip():
        (jdir / "changed_files.txt").write_text(changed)
        extra.append("- `changed_files.txt` — the FULL current text of every file the diff "
                     "touched. Use it when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a "
                     "criterion.")
    extra_block = ("\n" + "\n".join(extra)) if extra else ""
    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)

You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.

System contract:
{JUDGE_SYSTEM}

Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.{extra_block}

You are NOT given the task instruction, the reference/golden fix, the tests, or the rest of the
repository. Judge only what is here. If a criterion cannot be decided from these inputs, score it 0 — but note that a
criterion which is undecidable here is a defect in the rubric, not in the submission.

Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.

The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.

Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:

    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}

All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
""")


def build_user_prompt(criteria, diff: str, changed: str) -> str:
    """The API-backend counterpart of PROMPT.md, with the same inputs and exclusions.

    Deliberately withheld, exactly as in the sub-agent request: the task instruction, the
    golden fix.patch, tests/test.patch, and the screenshots. See the module docstring for
    why each one would corrupt the grade.
    """
    payload = json.dumps(
        [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria], indent=2
    )
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    parts = [
        "Grade the APPROACH of the code change below against each rubric criterion.",
        "",
        "## Criteria",
        payload,
        "",
        "## Candidate diff (test/spec/snapshot files already stripped)",
        "```diff",
        diff,
        "```",
    ]
    if changed.strip():
        parts += [
            "",
            "## Full current text of every file the diff touched",
            "Use this when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.",
            changed,
        ]
    parts += [
        "",
        "## Output",
        'Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences: {"scores": {"<id>": 0 or 1}}.',
        f"All {len(criteria)} ids must be present: {ids}.",
        "Score 1 only when the criterion is fully satisfied with clear evidence in the "
        "change; otherwise score 0. There is no partial credit.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def extract_scores_object(text: str):
    """Parse the model reply into a dict, tolerating fences and surrounding prose."""
    candidate = text.strip()
    if candidate.startswith("```"):
        candidate = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n?", "", candidate)
        candidate = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", candidate.strip())
    try:
        return json.loads(candidate)
    except Exception:
        pass
    start, depth = None, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(candidate):
        if ch == "{":
            if start is None:
                start = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == "}" and start is not None:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                try:
                    return json.loads(candidate[start : i + 1])
                except Exception:
                    start, depth = None, 0
    return None


def call_eval_api(criteria, diff: str, changed: str):
    """Grade via the proxy. Returns a scores-shaped dict, or None to fall back.

    Never raises: every failure path returns None so the caller can fall through to the
    sub-agent request and the run is never failed by the judge.
    """
    api_key = (os.environ.get("EVAL_API_KEY") or "").strip()
    base_url = (os.environ.get("EVAL_BASE_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
    model = (os.environ.get("EVAL_MODEL") or "").strip()
    if not api_key or not base_url or not model:
        sys.stderr.write(
            "[judge] API backend unavailable (EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL "
            "incomplete); falling back to the sub-agent request\n"
        )
        return None

    body = {
        "model": model,
        "temperature": 0,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": build_user_prompt(criteria, diff, changed)},
        ],
    }
    # The proxy attributes spend per `user`; without it this call is unattributable.
    if os.environ.get("EVAL_USER"):
        body["user"] = os.environ["EVAL_USER"]

    url = base_url + "/chat/completions"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    for attempt in range(1, API_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                url,
                data=data,
                method="POST",
                headers={
                    "Authorization": "Bearer %s" % api_key,
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                },
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=API_TIMEOUT_SEC) as resp:
                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            content = json.loads(raw)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            obj = extract_scores_object(content)
            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
                sys.stderr.write(
                    "[judge] attempt %d: reply was not JSON: %r\n" % (attempt, content[:400])
                )
            else:
                sys.stderr.write("[judge] graded via API model=%s\n" % model)
                return obj
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            detail = ""
            try:
                detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: HTTP %s %s\n" % (attempt, exc.code, detail)
            )
            # 4xx other than 429 will not fix themselves; stop retrying.
            if 400 <= exc.code < 500 and exc.code != 429:
                break
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: %s: %s\n" % (attempt, exc.__class__.__name__, exc)
            )
        if attempt < API_ATTEMPTS:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] API backend gave up; falling back to the sub-agent request\n")
    return None


def write_rubric_json(failed, total: int) -> None:
    """verifier.py reads this for rubric_failed_count."""
    try:
        Path(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with open(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, "w") as handle:
            json.dump({"failed": list(failed), "criteria_total": total}, handle, indent=2)
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not write %s: %s\n" % (RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, exc))


def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
    if not vp.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
        return None
    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
        return None
    failed, graded = [], 0
    for c in criteria:
        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
        if raw is None:
            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
            continue
        try:
            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            failed.append(c["id"])
            continue
        graded += 1
        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
            failed.append(c["id"])
    if graded == 0:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
        return None
    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
    ap.add_argument("--judge-dir", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    jdir = Path(a.judge_dir) if a.judge_dir else judge_dir()
    try:
        doc = json.load(open(a.rubrics))
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] cannot read %s: %s\n" % (a.rubrics, exc))
        return 0
    criteria = [c for c in (doc.get("criteria") or []) if c.get("id") and c.get("criterion")]
    if not criteria:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] no criteria in %s\n" % a.rubrics)
        return 0

    def emit(verdict, failed) -> int:
        """Publish a verdict: summary.json, rubric.json, then stdout LAST."""
        try:
            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
                       "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
                      open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
        except Exception:
            pass
        write_rubric_json(failed, len(criteria))
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
                         % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
        print(verdict)
        return 0

    # An existing verdict.json always wins: it is either a sub-agent verdict or this
    # script's own API result being rescored, and re-grading would cost a second call.
    res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
    if res is not None:
        return emit(*res)

    diff = candidate_diff(a.repo)
    if not diff.strip():
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] empty candidate diff; nothing to grade\n")
        return 0
    changed = collect_changed_files(a.repo, diff)

    # Preferred: grade in-band via the proxy. Persist the scores as verdict.json so the
    # grade is auditable and a rescore is idempotent, then score it through read_verdict
    # so both backends share one scoring path.
    scores = call_eval_api(criteria, diff, changed)
    if scores is not None:
        try:
            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (jdir / "verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(scores, indent=2))
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not persist verdict.json: %s\n" % exc)
        res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
        if res is not None:
            return emit(*res)
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] API verdict had no usable scores; writing the request\n")

    # Fallback: lay down the sub-agent request and stay silent.
    write_request(criteria, diff, jdir, changed=changed)
    sys.stderr.write(
        "[judge] no verdict at %s yet; wrote the judge request to %s (%s). Have the judge "
        "sub-agent produce verdict.json, then rescore. Scoring on tests alone until then.\n"
        % (jdir / "verdict.json", jdir, ", ".join(sorted(f.name for f in jdir.iterdir()))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

170	def changed_paths(diff: str) -> list:
171	    """Paths touched by the (already harness-filtered) diff, in order."""
172	    out = []
173	    for line in diff.splitlines():
174	        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
175	            parts = line.split()
176	            if len(parts) >= 4:
177	                p = parts[-1][2:]                  # strip the b/ prefix
178	                if p and p not in out:
179	                    out.append(p)

181	
182	
183	def collect_changed_files(repo: str, diff: str, budget: int = 200_000) -> str:
184	    """Full current text of every file the diff touched.
185	
186	    A hunk shows three lines of context, which is often too little to decide a criterion that
187	    is genuinely true of the change (e.g. "the helper is defined in the same module"). Whole
188	    files remove that class of false 0 while staying bounded by the size of the change.
189	    """
190	    blob, used = [], 0
191	    for rel in changed_paths(diff):
192	        fp = Path(repo) / rel
193	        if not fp.is_file():                       # deleted or renamed away
194	            continue
195	        try:
196	            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
197	        except Exception:
198	            continue
199	        chunk = "\n===== %s =====\n%s" % (rel, text)
200	        if used + len(chunk) > budget:
201	            blob.append("\n[... remaining changed files omitted for length ...]\n")
202	            break
203	        blob.append(chunk); used += len(chunk)
204	    return "".join(blob)
205	
206	
207	def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path, changed: str = "") -> None:
208	    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context."""
209	    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
210	    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
211	    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
212	    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff)
213	    extra = []
214	    if changed.strip():
215	        (jdir / "changed_files.txt").write_text(changed)
216	        extra.append("- `changed_files.txt` — the FULL current text of every file the diff "
217	                     "touched. Use it when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a "
218	                     "criterion.")
219	    extra_block = ("\n" + "\n".join(extra)) if extra else ""
220	    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
221	    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
222	    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)
223	
224	You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.
225	
226	System contract:
227	{JUDGE_SYSTEM}
228	
229	Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
230	- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
231	- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
232	  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.{extra_block}
233	
234	You are NOT given the task instruction, the reference/golden fix, the tests, or the rest of the
235	repository. Judge only what is here. If a criterion cannot be decided from these inputs, score it 0 — but note that a
236	criterion which is undecidable here is a defect in the rubric, not in the submission.
237	
238	Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
239	0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.
240	
241	The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
242	so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.
243	
244	Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:
245	
246	    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}
247	
248	All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
249	""")
250	
251	
252	def build_user_prompt(criteria, diff: str, changed: str) -> str:
253	    """The API-backend counterpart of PROMPT.md, with the same inputs and exclusions.
254	
255	    Deliberately withheld, exactly as in the sub-agent request: the task instruction, the
256	    golden fix.patch, tests/test.patch, and the screenshots. See the module docstring for
257	    why each one would corrupt the grade.
258	    """
259	    payload = json.dumps(
260	        [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria], indent=2
261	    )
262	    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
263	    parts = [
264	        "Grade the APPROACH of the code change below against each rubric criterion.",
265	        "",
266	        "## Criteria",
267	        payload,
268	        "",
269	        "## Candidate diff (test/spec/snapshot files already stripped)",
270	        "```diff",
271	        diff,
272	        "```",
273	    ]
274	    if changed.strip():
275	        parts += [
276	            "",
277	            "## Full current text of every file the diff touched",
278	            "Use this when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.",
279	            changed,
280	        ]
281	    parts += [
282	        "",
283	        "## Output",
284	        'Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences: {"scores": {"<id>": 0 or 1}}.',
285	        f"All {len(criteria)} ids must be present: {ids}.",
286	        "Score 1 only when the criterion is fully satisfied with clear evidence in the "
287	        "change; otherwise score 0. There is no partial credit.",
288	    ]
289	    return "\n".join(parts)
290	
291	
292	def extract_scores_object(text: str):
293	    """Parse the model reply into a dict, tolerating fences and surrounding prose."""
294	    candidate = text.strip()
295	    if candidate.startswith("```"):
296	        candidate = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n?", "", candidate)
297	        candidate = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", candidate.strip())
298	    try:
299	        return json.loads(candidate)
300	    except Exception:
301	        pass
302	    start, depth = None, 0
303	    for i, ch in enumerate(candidate):
304	        if ch == "{":
305	            if start is None:
306	                start = i
307	            depth += 1
308	        elif ch == "}" and start is not None:
309	            depth -= 1
310	            if depth == 0:
311	                try:
312	                    return json.loads(candidate[start : i + 1])
313	                except Exception:
314	                    start, depth = None, 0
315	    return None
316	
317	
318	def call_eval_api(criteria, diff: str, changed: str):
319	    """Grade via the proxy. Returns a scores-shaped dict, or None to fall back.
320	
321	    Never raises: every failure path returns None so the caller can fall through to the
322	    sub-agent request and the run is never failed by the judge.
323	    """
324	    api_key = (os.environ.get("EVAL_API_KEY") or "").strip()
325	    base_url = (os.environ.get("EVAL_BASE_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
326	    model = (os.environ.get("EVAL_MODEL") or "").strip()
327	    if not api_key or not base_url or not model:
328	        sys.stderr.write(
329	            "[judge] API backend unavailable (EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL "
330	            "incomplete); falling back to the sub-agent request\n"
331	        )
332	        return None
333	
334	    body = {
335	        "model": model,
336	        "temperature": 0,
337	        "messages": [
338	            {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
339	            {"role": "user", "content": build_user_prompt(criteria, diff, changed)},
340	        ],
341	    }
342	    # The proxy attributes spend per `user`; without it this call is unattributable.
343	    if os.environ.get("EVAL_USER"):
344	        body["user"] = os.environ["EVAL_USER"]
345	
346	    url = base_url + "/chat/completions"
347	    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
348	    for attempt in range(1, API_ATTEMPTS + 1):
349	        try:
350	            req = urllib.request.Request(
351	                url,
352	                data=data,
353	                method="POST",
354	                headers={
355	                    "Authorization": "Bearer %s" % api_key,
356	                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
357	                },
358	            )
359	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=API_TIMEOUT_SEC) as resp:
360	                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
361	            content = json.loads(raw)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
362	            obj = extract_scores_object(content)
363	            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
364	                sys.stderr.write(
365	                    "[judge] attempt %d: reply was not JSON: %r\n" % (attempt, content[:400])
366	                )
367	            else:
368	                sys.stderr.write("[judge] graded via API model=%s\n" % model)
369	                return obj
370	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
371	            detail = ""
372	            try:
373	                detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
374	            except Exception:
375	                pass
376	            sys.stderr.write(
377	                "[judge] attempt %d: HTTP %s %s\n" % (attempt, exc.code, detail)
378	            )
379	            # 4xx other than 429 will not fix themselves; stop retrying.
380	            if 400 <= exc.code < 500 and exc.code != 429:
381	                break
382	        except Exception as exc:
383	            sys.stderr.write(
384	                "[judge] attempt %d: %s: %s\n" % (attempt, exc.__class__.__name__, exc)
385	            )
386	        if attempt < API_ATTEMPTS:
387	            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
388	    sys.stderr.write("[judge] API backend gave up; falling back to the sub-agent request\n")
389	    return None
390	
391	
392	def write_rubric_json(failed, total: int) -> None:
393	    """verifier.py reads this for rubric_failed_count."""
394	    try:
395	        Path(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
396	        with open(RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, "w") as handle:
397	            json.dump({"failed": list(failed), "criteria_total": total}, handle, indent=2)
398	    except OSError as exc:
399	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not write %s: %s\n" % (RUBRIC_JSON_PATH, exc))
400	
401	
402	def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
403	    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
404	    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
405	    if not vp.is_file():
406	        return None
407	    try:
408	        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
409	    except Exception as exc:
410	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
411	        return None
412	    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
413	    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
414	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
415	        return None
416	    failed, graded = [], 0
417	    for c in criteria:
418	        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
419	        if raw is None:
420	            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
421	            continue
422	        try:
423	            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
424	        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
425	            failed.append(c["id"])
426	            continue
427	        graded += 1
428	        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
429	            failed.append(c["id"])
430	    if graded == 0:
431	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
432	        return None
433	    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed
434	
435	
436	def main() -> int:
437	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
438	    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
439	    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
440	    ap.add_argument("--judge-dir", default=None)
441	    a = ap.parse_args()
442	
443	    jdir = Path(a.judge_dir) if a.judge_dir else judge_dir()
444	    try:
445	        doc = json.load(open(a.rubrics))
446	    except Exception as exc:
447	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] cannot read %s: %s\n" % (a.rubrics, exc))
448	        return 0
449	    criteria = [c for c in (doc.get("criteria") or []) if c.get("id") and c.get("criterion")]
450	    if not criteria:
451	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] no criteria in %s\n" % a.rubrics)
452	        return 0
453	
454	    def emit(verdict, failed) -> int:
455	        """Publish a verdict: summary.json, rubric.json, then stdout LAST."""
456	        try:
457	            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
458	            json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
459	                       "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
460	                      open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
461	        except Exception:
462	            pass
463	        write_rubric_json(failed, len(criteria))
464	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
465	                         % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
466	        print(verdict)
467	        return 0
468	
469	    # An existing verdict.json always wins: it is either a sub-agent verdict or this
470	    # script's own API result being rescored, and re-grading would cost a second call.
471	    res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
472	    if res is not None:
473	        return emit(*res)
474	
475	    diff = candidate_diff(a.repo)
476	    if not diff.strip():
477	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] empty candidate diff; nothing to grade\n")
478	        return 0
479	    changed = collect_changed_files(a.repo, diff)
480	
481	    # Preferred: grade in-band via the proxy. Persist the scores as verdict.json so the
482	    # grade is auditable and a rescore is idempotent, then score it through read_verdict
483	    # so both backends share one scoring path.
484	    scores = call_eval_api(criteria, diff, changed)
485	    if scores is not None:
486	        try:
487	            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
488	            (jdir / "verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(scores, indent=2))
489	        except OSError as exc:
490	            sys.stderr.write("[judge] could not persist verdict.json: %s\n" % exc)
491	        res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
492	        if res is not None:
493	            return emit(*res)
494	        sys.stderr.write("[judge] API verdict had no usable scores; writing the request\n")
495	
496	    # Fallback: lay down the sub-agent request and stay silent.
497	    write_request(criteria, diff, jdir, changed=changed)
498	    sys.stderr.write(
499	        "[judge] no verdict at %s yet; wrote the judge request to %s (%s). Have the judge "
500	        "sub-agent produce verdict.json, then rescore. Scoring on tests alone until then.\n"
501	        % (jdir / "verdict.json", jdir, ", ".join(sorted(f.name for f in jdir.iterdir()))))
502	    return 0
503	
504	
505	if __name__ == "__main__":
